title: Seeding the main stack
statement: Let $c$ be a program in the partial-recursive language and let $x$ be a Boolean string. Starting from the scanning state at input-head position $|x|+1$, with all stacks and the output empty, exactly three steps of the bridging machine lead to the backward-reading state at input-head position $|x|$. The main stack then contains the sentinel true-bit symbol followed by the list terminator; the other stacks and output remain empty.
hypotheses_covered: A program $c$ in the partial-recursive language
replaced:
From the bridge configuration of the bridging machine in the scanning state at the
right endmarker of the embedded Boolean input $x$ (all stacks empty, empty output),
exactly three steps lead to the backward-reading state with the input head at
position $\abs{x}$ and the main stack holding just the sentinel true-bit symbol on
top of the list terminator, the other stacks empty and the output empty.
